heading: plot cleared for the year
body:
Got the last of the old bean sticks out and the plot is bare now, just the perennial corner left as it is. Ground is heavier than I remembered, took most of the afternoon to turn even half of it over. Left the rest for next weekend, arms not what they were.

Rhubarb crowns are already pushing up a bit which is encouraging after such a wet winter. Path along the top edge needs re-laying too, the bark chips have mostly washed away into the grass over the wet months, but that can wait until the beds are sorted.

heading: ground still too wet to get on
body:
Tried to get the spade in on the top bed and it just squelched, no good doing anything with it yet. Going to leave it another week or two and hope for a dry spell. Meanwhile sorted the shed out a bit, found three half used packets of carrot seed from two years back, not sure if they'll still come up.

Also found a bag of onion sets gone soft and green at the neck, straight in the compost. Need to make a proper list of what's actually usable before I buy anything new this year, easy to duplicate without meaning to.

heading: potatoes go in the top bed every year, that's settled now
body:
Had the same discussion with myself as every spring and I'm done moving it about — the top bed gets the potatoes, full stop, it's the sunniest and it drains best once the winter wet clears. No more trying other spots to see if it's better somewhere else, it never is. Chitting starts in the porch from late this month, egg boxes propped on the windowsill like always.

Wrote it on the inside of the shed door as well so I stop second-guessing myself when the seed catalogue turns up with pictures of some other bed doing wonders.

heading: slugs found the lettuce already
body:
First proper sowing of lettuce and within a week half of it had gone, just stalks left standing where whole seedlings should have been. Didn't even get to see a proper leaf on some of them before they disappeared overnight. Should have put something down straight away instead of waiting to see if it was going to be a problem this year, it is always a problem in that corner.

Going to try again with a fresh sowing further along the bed, away from the damp patch by the path, and put something down round it from day one this time rather than after the damage is already done.

heading: potatoes chitting on the kitchen windowsill
body:
Eyes coming up nicely on the earlies, another couple of weeks and they'll be ready to go in the ground. Windowsill is a bit crowded, might have to move some of the trays to the spare room which won't go down well with anyone else in the house.

Bought a new bag of maincrop seed potatoes too, a different variety this year on a recommendation from someone at the site who swears by it for keeping well over winter. We'll see how it compares to the usual one once it's up and cropping.

heading: not sure the drainage on the top bed is right
body:
Water was still sitting on the surface of the top bed two days after the last proper rain, which doesn't seem right for a bed that's supposed to drain well and always has done before. Could be that the path running along the side is compacting the soil right next to it and forming a bit of a lip that traps the water in.

Haven't actually looked into what to do about it, just noted it down while I was standing there in wellies wondering whether to bother digging in that section today at all.

heading: leave the compost heap alone and it still heats up fine on its own
body:
Been letting the heap just sit this year rather than turning it every few weeks like I used to bother with, and it still got properly warm in the middle, steam coming off it on a cold morning when I lifted the lid to add the kitchen scraps. Saves a fair bit of effort not forking it all over on a Sunday.

Might just be luck with what's gone into it this particular year, a good mix of grass clippings and cardboard from the moving boxes, but it seems to be working well enough that I'm not going to bother changing anything.

heading: parsnips never came up again, don't know why
body:
Third year running and barely a seedling from the parsnip row, same as the last two attempts however carefully I try to sow them. Same seed packet as everyone else on the site seems to manage perfectly well with, so it's not obviously a bad batch. Could be the seed is simply too old by the time I get round to sowing it, could be the ground's not fine enough where I put it in.

Not got to the bottom of it and honestly not sure I ever will, might just accept parsnips aren't for this plot and buy them from the greengrocer like a sensible person.

heading: the shady end is fine for tomatoes, plenty of light gets in
body:
Decided the tomatoes are going in the shady bed by the fence this year after going back and forth on it for a couple of weeks. Watched it over a few afternoons and the sun does come round by midday and stays on it for a good few hours, more than I originally thought it would given how it looks in the morning.

Saves the sunny bed for the squash which need the room to spread anyway and would only shade the tomatoes out regardless. That's where the tomatoes are going from now on, no more chopping and changing every spring.

heading: broad beans through, look strong
body:
Rows are up and sturdy already, no sign of the mice getting at them this time which has been a real problem in previous years, whole rows gone before they even broke the surface. Staked the ends of the row so they don't flop about once they get taller and the pods start to weigh the stems down.

A few gaps where nothing came up at all, filled those in with spares I'd started off in pots as insurance, worth doing every year even though it feels like a faff at the time.

heading: blackfly all over the broad bean tips
body:
Went down to check on the beans and the top few inches of every plant is thick black with them, worse than I've seen it before on this row. Should have pinched the tops out as soon as the first flowers set like I keep telling myself to do every single year and then forgetting.

Sprayed with soapy water and squashed what I could reach by hand, we'll see how much good it does. Half wondering whether the mild spring just suited them better than usual.

heading: netting the brassicas the day they go in keeps the pigeons off every time
body:
Put the net over the young cabbages the same afternoon I planted them out rather than waiting a few days like I used to when I thought they'd be too small to bother a pigeon, and not a single peck mark on them this time. The times I've lost a whole row before it's always because I left it a day or two thinking they'd be fine that first night.

Doing it straight away now as a rule, net and pegs ready in the wheelbarrow before I even put the first plant in the ground.

heading: onion sets in, mulched with grass clippings
body:
Got the sets in along the usual row, pushed them in just so the tips show above the soil like the packet says. Put a layer of grass clippings from the mow round them to keep the weeds down and hold a bit of moisture in, seems to be working so far and looks tidier than bare soil.

Weather's turned properly mild this week, first time it's felt like spring rather than a cold snap pretending to be spring, and the whole plot smells different for it.

heading: compost heap still not hot in the middle, not sure what's wrong with it
body:
Put my hand in and it's barely warm, nothing like it should be by now going on past years. Might be too much of the woody prunings in there from the hedge cutting and not enough green stuff to balance it out properly.

Been meaning to sort it out properly, fork it all out and rebuild it with a better mix, but keep just adding to the top instead of actually fixing the pile underneath. Easier to add than to unpick, which is probably why it never gets done.

heading: strawberry runners pegged down for new plants
body:
Pegged half a dozen of the strongest runners into small pots sunk in the ground next to the parent plants, should have decent new crowns by the autumn to fill the gaps at the end of the bed where a couple died off over winter. Left the rest of the runners to be cut off so the main plants keep their energy for fruiting rather than spreading everywhere.

Bed's looking a bit tired overall, might be time to think about starting a fresh one in a couple of years once these are established.

heading: asparagus bed stays put, not digging it up
body:
Had a think about whether it's worth the space it takes up for what it actually gives back each year, but decided against digging it up for now. It's cropping reasonably well now it's established, and starting from scratch again would mean a couple of years with nothing at all from that whole bed while new crowns settle in.

Leaving it be, at least for this season, and going to see how the harvest is once it's properly into its stride before thinking about it again.

heading: slugs back on the lettuce again
body:
Second sowing and the same story as before, chewed to nothing within days of germinating, same bed as the first lot. Put slug pellets down this time which I said I wasn't going to bother with after last year, but the eggshells clearly aren't doing enough on their own in that particular corner.

Starting to wonder if it's just not worth sowing lettuce there at all until I sort the drainage and the damp out properly, but haven't got round to moving it yet.

heading: raised beds for the brassicas from now on, easier to net
body:
Built two raised beds along the back fence over the weekend and moving all the brassicas there permanently rather than rotating them round the open beds like before. Much easier to get a net taut and pegged down properly on a raised bed than trying to drape it over open ground where the pigeons always seem to find the gaps at the corners.

Took longer than expected to build, borrowed a drill off someone at the site, but worth it if it finally keeps the cabbages whole this year.

heading: first courgette flowers open
body:
Bright yellow flowers out on the courgette plants already, no fruit set yet but it won't be long going by how fast they usually go once they get started. Always amazes me how quickly they turn from a small seedling into something taking over half the bed.

Put a bit of extra compost round the base of each plant while I was down there, they're hungry things and it's easy to forget to feed them once the leaves get big enough to hide the soil.

heading: eggshells round the lettuce keep the slugs down a bit
body:
Crushed up a season's worth of eggshells and scattered them thick around the new lettuce seedlings as soon as they were big enough to handle it. Not a complete fix, still lost a couple of plants at the edge where the ring wasn't thick enough, but nowhere near as bad as the row last year with nothing round it at all.

Worth the bother even if it's not perfect, and it uses up shells that would otherwise just go in the food bin.

heading: lost a tray of seedlings to a late frost, forgot to fleece them
body:
Left a tray of squash seedlings out overnight thinking we were past the frosts by that point in the year, didn't check the forecast properly or maybe didn't check it at all if I'm honest with myself. Whole tray was black and flopped over by the morning, every single one gone.

Had to start again from a fresh packet of seed, lost the best part of three weeks getting back to where I'd been, and felt fairly stupid about it walking round the plot that day.

heading: rhubarb ready to pull
body:
Stalks are thick and a good deep colour now, pulled the first bundle today for a crumble which went down well. Left the smaller ones near the middle of the crown to bulk up a bit more before taking any more.

Plant looks better than it has done in a couple of years, glad I gave it a good mulch of manure back in the autumn, seems to have made a real difference.

heading: leeks look pale, could be the soil or could be leek moth
body:
The leek row has gone a washed-out yellowy green rather than the usual dark blue-green they normally have by this point. Might just be nitrogen, could be something going on at the roots that I haven't seen yet.

Haven't dug one up to actually have a proper look, keep meaning to on the way past but end up doing something else instead. Going to try and make myself do it next time I'm down there rather than just walking by and frowning at them again.

heading: no bonfires after six, committee rule, fair enough
body:
New rule came round at the last meeting, no burning after six in the evening because of the smoke drifting into the houses backing onto the site and the complaints that had been coming in about it. Grumbled a bit at the time, mostly because evenings are when I've got the time to do it, but honestly it's a reasonable ask.

Just means planning the bonfire pile for a morning instead, which suits the weekend visits better anyway once I got used to the idea.

heading: cabbages hearting up now the net's on
body:
The cabbages on the new raised bed are starting to firm up properly in the middle, first time in a while one hasn't been half stripped before it got the chance to actually heart up. Net's doing its job so far, pegged down all round with no gaps I can find.

A couple of the outer leaves have got a bit of caterpillar damage where something must have got in before the net went on, but nothing serious enough to worry about.

heading: sowing lettuce a few seeds at a time every couple of weeks means there's always some ready
body:
Instead of putting a whole row in at once and having it all bolt together in the same week like it used to, I've been doing a short row every fortnight or so along the same section. Means there's always something at the right stage to pick and nothing sitting there going to seed before I get round to eating it.

Bit more effort to remember when the last sowing was, keeping a note on the back of the shed door helps, but it's worth it for not wasting whole rows of lettuce to bolting any more.

heading: still don't know why the sweet peas won't climb properly
body:
Put them up against the same wigwam of canes as always and they just flop about at the base instead of twining up neatly like they're supposed to do once they get going. Wondered whether the canes are too smooth this year or spaced too far apart for the tendrils to catch hold of properly.

Haven't tried anything different to see if it makes a difference, just watching them flop about every time I walk past and feeling a bit sorry for them, which isn't much of a plan.

heading: tomatoes went into the shady bed like always
body:
Planted the tomatoes out in their usual spot by the fence today, staked them well and watered in properly to settle the roots in. Squash going in the sunny bed as planned, plenty of room there for them to spread out over the summer without swamping anything else.

A couple of the tomato plants looked a bit leggy already from being indoors too long, hardened them off a few extra days but might not have been quite enough.

heading: lettuce hit by slugs yet again, third time this year
body:
Pellets and eggshells both down round the row and still lost a good third of it overnight, worse than either of the previous sowings this year even with everything I've tried. Starting to think the lettuce bed itself is just a slug highway of some kind, something about being close to the damp corner by the water butt that draws them in.

Might have to move the whole row entirely next year to somewhere further from that corner rather than keep fighting it in the same spot.

heading: fleece over the carrots the first fortnight keeps the fly off, works every year
body:
Same trick as always, fleece pinned down tight over the carrot row as soon as they're sown and left on until the seedlings are a decent size and less likely to attract attention. Never had carrot fly get to them since I started doing this a few years back, touch wood every time I say it.

Takes about ten minutes to put on and the same to take off again later, small price for a clean row of carrots at the end of it.

heading: runner beans up the canes nicely
body:
Beans have found the canes on their own this year without needing much tying in at all, twining up well already and looking healthy along the whole row. Flowers just starting to show at the base of the plants, bright red against the green.

Should be picking by midsummer if the weather holds, put a bit of mulch round the base to help keep the moisture in while they're setting pods.

heading: meant to sort the water butt out weeks ago, still haven't
body:
The tap on the water butt by the lettuce bed has been dripping constantly since spring, wasting whatever gets collected and keeping that whole corner permanently damp whatever the weather's doing otherwise. Keep saying I'll get a new washer for it from the hardware shop and keep not actually doing it.

It's a small thing on its own but it's probably not helping with the slug problem in that bed either, everything considered.

heading: sweetcorn going in, a bit later than planned
body:
Got the sweetcorn plants in today, later than I meant to get round to it but the block they're going into should still catch up given how warm it's been the last week or so. Planted in a proper block rather than a single row like last time, meant to help with the pollination once the tassels come.

Watered each one in well and put a slug barrier round the smaller plants while they establish, learned that lesson elsewhere this year.

heading: changed my mind about the asparagus bed, digging it up this autumn
body:
Said back in the spring I was leaving the asparagus bed as it is for at least this season, but the crop's been thin again this year and it's taking up a good chunk of space for what it actually gives back at harvest. Going to dig it out properly once it's died back for the winter and use the space for something that earns its keep a bit better.

Feels like a waste of a few years' patience getting it established in the first place, but no point keeping something going out of stubbornness alone.

heading: tomatoes in the shady bed have gone leggy, barely any fruit on them
body:
The tomato plants by the fence are tall and thin with hardly a truss setting properly, nothing like the ones a neighbour further along has got growing in full sun on the other side of the site. That bed clearly doesn't get anywhere near as much light as I convinced myself it did back in the spring when I was standing there watching it for a few afternoons.

Wasted the whole first half of the season on the wrong spot for them, should have trusted what the plants themselves were telling me a lot sooner than I did.

heading: marrow taking over, huge one hiding under the leaves
body:
Found a marrow the size of a rugby ball under the courgette leaves today that must have been sitting there a good week or more without me noticing it at all. Too big to do much with now except stuff it and share the rest with whoever will take it off my hands.

Going to check the plants properly every couple of days from now on rather than just glancing over them on the way to somewhere else, easy to lose track of how fast they grow.

heading: still haven't decided what to do with the far end past the shed
body:
It's been empty or half used all season again, tried a few different things there over the years and none of it has really come to anything worth mentioning. Too shaded for most of the summer crops, too dry in a hot spell because of the shed roof catching the rain before it reaches the ground.

Keeps coming up in my head every time I walk down there and I keep putting off actually deciding on it properly, probably because none of the obvious answers feel quite right.

heading: comfrey feed once a week and the tomatoes clearly like it
body:
Been cutting the comfrey down by the fence and steeping it in a bucket for a liquid feed, giving the tomatoes and the courgettes a dose of it once a week through the growing season. Growth and fruit set both noticeably better on the fed plants compared to a couple I forgot to do for a fortnight while I was away.

Smells fairly dreadful once it's had a few days to steep properly, but it clearly does the job and costs nothing beyond the bucket and a lid to keep the worst of the smell in.

heading: beetroot doing well, pulling a few at a time
body:
Pulling the beetroot as golf ball sized ones rather than waiting for them to get bigger, seem sweeter and less woody that way than leaving them to grow on. Row's holding up well overall, no sign of the leaf miner that got into them a couple of years back and ruined most of the crop.

Leaves are good in a salad too, easy to forget you can eat those as well as the root itself.

heading: a barrier of grit round the strawberries keeps the slugs off better than the pellets did
body:
Laid a thick ring of horticultural grit around each strawberry plant a few weeks back and it's made a real difference, fruit coming through mostly clean this year with far fewer of the chewed ones I usually end up composting. Slugs don't seem keen on crossing it.

Better than the pellets ever managed on their own for this particular bed, though it took a fair bit of grit to do the whole row properly and a trip to the builders' merchant to get enough.

heading: lettuce and the slugs again, giving up and going to pellets properly this time
body:
Another sowing gone overnight in that same corner, same bed, same story as every other attempt this year regardless of what I've tried around it. Done trying the gentler options for this particular spot, just putting pellets down from the start from now on rather than waiting to see if it's actually needed.

Might finally move the lettuce somewhere else entirely next year, but for the rest of this season it's pellets and hoping for the best.

heading: not sure if it's worth keeping the rhubarb where it is, might be too shaded now
body:
The tree next door on the other plot has filled out a lot over the last couple of years and the rhubarb corner doesn't get the morning sun it used to get when it was first put in. Stalks seemed a bit thinner than usual this year compared to previous seasons.

Haven't actually measured anything or timed how much sun reaches it now, just a feeling looking at it most times I walk past, which isn't much to go on but it's stuck with me all the same.

heading: no more direct sowing carrots, always module raise them now
body:
Decided after yet another patchy, gappy row that direct sowing carrots straight into the ground isn't worth the bother any more, too easy to lose them to slugs or poor germination before they're even properly up. Starting them in modules in the cold frame instead and planting out as small plants once they've got a bit of size to them.

Apparently helps with carrot fly too according to a few people at the site, though the main reason is just not wasting a whole row of seed on nothing coming up.

heading: not sure if the netting on the currants is enough once the frost starts
body:
The net's kept the birds off well enough through the summer while the fruit was ripening, but I don't know if it does anything useful once the cold weather comes and everything else on the site the birds might want has gone for the winter. Might just end up being in the way rather than doing anything useful by then.

Need to look at it again nearer the time rather than just leaving it up all winter and assuming it's still helping.

heading: digging the first earlies, decent size
body:
Forked up the first row of earlies today, good size on most of them, a few small ones near the end of the row but nothing to complain about given the season. Sacks going in the shed to dry off a bit before storing them properly.

Skins are still thin enough to bruise easily, handled them carefully carrying the trug back up the path so as not to knock too many about.

heading: turning the compost every few weeks is what actually gets it hot, leaving it alone does nothing
body:
Started forking the heap over properly every few weeks instead of the leave-it-be approach I was doing earlier in the year, and it's steaming within a couple of days each time now, proper heat right through the middle when I check it with my hand. Whatever I thought was working before clearly wasn't doing very much at all.

More effort than just piling stuff on top and walking away, but the difference in how quickly it's breaking down is obvious enough that it's worth the extra forking.

heading: garlic going in where the courgettes came out
body:
Cleared the spent courgette plants today and got the garlic cloves in straight after, want them settled in before the ground gets too cold to work easily. Bulbs from a friend's saved crop rather than bought sets this time, hoping they take just as well.

Bed's had a good dose of compost dug in first, courgettes are hungry things and take a fair bit out of the soil by the end of a season.

heading: squash mildew came on fast this week, whole leaf gone white in two days
body:
Noticed a dusting on one leaf on the Monday and by the Wednesday half the plant was covered in it, spreading faster than anything I've seen on there before. Should have cut the affected leaves off straight away instead of waiting to see if it spread on its own, of course it did, mildew always does once it gets a foothold.

Cut the worst of it back now and given the rest a spray, hoping it hasn't set the plant back too badly this late in the season.

heading: sweetcorn tasselling
body:
Tassels out on the sweetcorn now, block planting seems to have done its job well, plenty of pollen about when I brushed a hand across the top of the plants. Should know in a few weeks whether the cobs have filled out properly or not.

Staked a couple of the taller plants at the edge of the block where the wind's been catching them more than the ones sheltered in the middle.

heading: there's a bare patch under the apple tree that never grows anything right
body:
Tried a few different things there over the years, nothing ever does particularly well, comes up thin and pale compared to the rest of the plot even with the same care given to it. Could be the roots taking everything out of the soil before anything else gets a look in, could be the soil itself is just poor under there.

Keep meaning to get it looked at properly and never quite get round to it, always something else more urgent to deal with elsewhere on the plot first.

heading: changed my mind about the potato bed, they're going in the bottom bed from now on
body:
Said for years the top bed was the place for potatoes and that was settled for good, but scab's got into that bed now and it's not worth the risk of it building up further year on year. Moving them to the bottom bed from next spring instead, the top can have beans instead which should help clean the ground up a bit while it rests from potatoes.

Feels odd changing a rule I've stuck to for so long, but there's no point being stubborn about it once the soil's telling you something different.

heading: blackberries ripening along the fence
body:
First of the blackberries turning properly dark and sweet along the back fence, picking a handful most times I'm down there now on the way past. The birds are getting their fair share too but there's still plenty to go round for everyone.

Cut back some of the more rampant growth reaching into the path while I was there, they'll take over the whole walkway if left entirely to their own devices.

heading: left the greenhouse door shut on a hot day, cooked the young plants inside
body:
Warm morning turned into a proper scorcher by early afternoon and I'd shut the door and vents that morning thinking rain was coming in off the forecast I half remembered. Went down later in the day and the young plants inside were completely wilted flat, lost a whole tray of them for good.

Meant to check the actual forecast properly before closing everything up rather than going on a guess, didn't, and paid for it with a tray of seedlings I'll have to start again.

heading: picking the beans every couple of days keeps them cropping, stop and they stop too
body:
Noticed the runner beans slow right down whenever I go more than a few days without picking them properly, the plant seems to decide it's done its job once a few pods are left on to swell and toughen up rather than being taken young. Keeping on top of it every couple of days and they just keep coming steadily.

Easy to let it slip when there's other things going on, but the difference in how much comes off the row is noticeable within a week either way.

heading: clearing the bean rows
body:
Pulled the spent bean plants and canes today, roots left in the ground to rot down and feed the soil like always rather than pulling the whole lot out. Ground looks tired after a full season of cropping, going to get some compost worked into it before it's properly done for the year.

Canes cleaned off and stacked in the shed for next spring, a job that always takes longer than it should.

heading: shady bed is never getting tomatoes again
body:
After this year's leggy, barely-fruiting lot by the fence I'm done pretending that bed gets enough sun for tomatoes, whatever it looked like on those few afternoons back in spring when I talked myself into it. Sun beds only for them from now on, whatever else has to move to make room for it.

Wish I'd trusted what I could see with my own eyes back then instead of convincing myself otherwise because it was convenient for the rest of the layout.

heading: leaves turning, apples ready
body:
Apples on the tree are colouring up well and a few have already started dropping, which usually means the rest aren't far behind them. Picked a bagful for now, more to come over the next couple of weeks as they ripen further.

Started a mental list of who on the site might want some, always more than we can use ourselves in one go.

heading: onions rotted where they'd been planted too close together
body:
Lifted the onions today and a good third of them had gone soft in the middle, mostly the ones packed in tightly along one end of the row where I'd squeezed a few extra sets in back in spring without really thinking it through. Air clearly wasn't getting round them properly in that section.

Spacing them out properly next time, no more squeezing extras in just because there was a gap that looked like it could fit one more.

heading: netting the currant bushes keeps the birds off, works well
body:
Same net I use most years, draped and pegged down properly before the fruit starts to colour up rather than waiting until it's obviously ripe and already too late. Kept the blackbirds off almost entirely this time round.

The one year I left it a bit late putting it up they'd had half the crop before I even noticed anything was missing, so it's become a fixed job on the calendar now rather than something I remember when I happen to think of it.

heading: not bothering with a greenhouse this year, the cold frame does enough
body:
Thought about getting a proper greenhouse after losing that tray of plants in the heat earlier in the year, but decided the cold frame and a bit more care with the vents does what's needed for the scale of what I actually grow here. No point paying for more space than I'd use.

Saves the cost and the space on the plot for something else instead, maybe another raised bed along the fence where the old shed used to stand.
